clue.text: Monsieur whose French is evergreen

parts.note: in French, 'whose?' is asked as 'à qui?'

explanation.surface: A puzzle over which Frenchman a certain evergreen belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent on 'à qui' is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The maqui is a Chilean shrub that keeps its leaves all year, an example of an evergreen.

clue.text: Again accept one's right in the world of Lord Butler?

indicators.note: signals that the letter goes inside the phrase for the world

parts.note: the politician R. A. Butler was known as Rab, so his world is RAB'S ORB

indicators.note: the right-hand side of a word is its final letter, so this takes the end of the word one

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a person is free to readmit something in Rab Butler's sphere.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab Butler was a senior British Conservative minister of the mid-20th century, always called Rab from his initials. E, the right-hand letter of 'one', goes inside RABSORB.
explanation.definitionFit: To reabsorb is to take something in once more, a synonym for accepting it again.

clue.text: Old rival of Athens bit into it

indicators.note: signals one piece going inside the other, here the bit going into it

parts.note: 'it' is crossword slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a bit of something is a part of it

explanation.surface: A historical fragment about some rival of Athens taking a bite out of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' reads as the past tense of bite, but it is the noun meaning a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was the great Greek city-state that fought Athens in the Peloponnesian War.

clue.text: Late summer period that presages –e stor-?

definitions.text: Late summer period that presages –e stor-?

parts.words: Late summer period that presages –e stor-?
parts.note: the dashes show a well-known saying about calm before bad weather, its noun clipped at both ends; clip the calm the same way and you have the month that comes before

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster's note about a calm late-summer spell before a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: The idea is 'the lull before the storm': strip TH and the final letter from THE LULL, just as '–e stor-' strips them from THE STORM, and the Hebrew month is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Elul is the sixth month of the Jewish calendar, falling in August and September, so a late summer period.

clue.text: Pad's a bit steep when going upstairs?

parts.note: a jot is a tiny amount

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: to ret flax is to steep or soak it

explanation.surface: Someone's flat is a little steep on the climb to the upper floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pad' and 'steep' both suggest housing and climbing; they are a notebook and soaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small notebook, the same as a writing pad.

clue.text: Go for a hash, perhaps — seasoned Caribbean stew

parts.note: go in the sense of energy or vigour is pep
per means for each, for a, as in 'per head'
hash, short for hashish, is an example of pot, cannabis

explanation.surface: A cook deciding to make a hash and ending with a spicy Caribbean stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hash' looks like a cooked dish beside 'stew', but it is the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperpot is a spicy meat stew from the West Indies, especially Guyana.

clue.text: Diuretic medication? Father William's mixed up caps!

indicators.note: the caps are the initial letters of the two words, which change places

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old schoolboy slang, for father
Will is the short form of William

explanation.surface: Someone shouting that old Father William has got his hats muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first letters of PATER and WILL and you get WATER PILL. 'caps' hints at headgear but means the leading letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A water pill is the everyday name for a diuretic, a drug that makes the body lose fluid.

clue.text: One picks up purse after fighting dog

definitions.text: One picks up purse after fighting
definitions.meaning: a professional prizefighter collects the prize money, the purse, after a bout

explanation.surface: Someone collects a handbag after a scuffle involving a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is a fighter paid a purse, and a boxer is also a stocky German breed of hound.

clue.text: Realise, after looking up 'seborrhoea' — not a word!

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up reads the word from the bottom upward, backwards

parts.note: seborrhoea, oily skin, is linked to acne
sh! is the call for silence, not a word

explanation.surface: Someone discovers, after checking a dictionary for a medical term, that it isn't a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking up' suggests a dictionary search; in a down clue it turns ACNE over.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to convert it to money, which is to encash it.

clue.text: Masseuse played games

definitions.meaning: in bridge or whist a ... is a set of games played

explanation.surface: A masseuse who was playing games with her clients.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber is one who massages, and also a contest of several games in cards.

clue.text: Oscar's cut ineptly working printing machine

indicators.note: Oscar has cut into the other letters, so he goes inside them
working on letters reshapes them, so ineptly is rearranged

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Oscar has made a clumsy cut on a working printing press.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside an arrangement of INEPTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Linotype was a hot-metal typesetting machine that cast whole lines of type for printing.

clue.text: Red Teletubby preferred to yellow, it's rumoured, in Hollywood country

indicators.note: one thing preferred to another takes its place, so one name replaces the other

parts.note: La La Land is a nickname for Los Angeles and its film world, Hollywood

indicators.note: rumour is what people say, so the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Laa-Laa is the yellow Teletubby
Po is the red Teletubby

explanation.surface: A child's TV fan explaining which Teletubby is the favourite in Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Teletubbies are a BBC toddlers' show with four coloured characters. 'it's rumoured' means the yellow one's name is matched by its sound inside the Hollywood nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Poland is a nation of central Europe, so a country.

clue.text: Money that will be needed in audition

definitions.text: that will be needed in audition

explanation.surface: Cash a performer must bring along to an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition only works when spoken: what will be kneaded is bread dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is informal for cash, and it is also the mixture a baker works with the hands.

clue.text: Dual gold rings are reportedly a shade of orange

indicators.note: the two golds ring, or surround, the next piece

parts.note: gold twice: AU is the chemical symbol and OR the heraldic term

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: the word are spoken sounds like the letter R

explanation.surface: A jeweller describing two gold rings as a particular orange tint.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold has two crossword forms, the chemical symbol and the heraldic tincture; 'rings' has both of them round the letter that 'are' sounds like.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora is the name of a rosy orange-pink colour, after the dawn goddess and the glow of daybreak.

clue.text: Is salt, say, rigging ____?

indicators.note: rigging something fixes or rearranges it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor's riddle asking what a salt, an old seaman, is rigging.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is the answer: a salt rigging staysails, and the letters of IS SALT SAY rearranged make them.
explanation.definitionFit: Staysails are fore-and-aft sails set on the stays of a ship, part of what a sailor rigs.

clue.text: Range of aeroplane-minicab journey?

parts.note: the hyphenated word runs from letter A to letter B

explanation.surface: Asking how far a combined plane and taxi trip can go.
explanation.walkthrough: The range of the word 'aeroplane-minicab' is from its first letter to its last.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting from A to B is the idiom for a simple journey between two places.

clue.text: Hooligan appeared, carrying nude

indicators.note: a nude figure is stripped of its outer covering, so the word loses its outside letters

parts.note: to arrive carrying something is to have brought it

explanation.surface: A thug turned up holding a naked figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nude' strips the outer B and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a violent, disorderly person, the same as a hooligan or ruffian.

clue.text: Was top cop bad?

parts.note: someone in charge of an organisation ran it
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, stands in for police detectives

explanation.surface: Asking whether the senior police officer was corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the detective branch of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid food has gone off, so it is bad.

clue.text: Fine start to day, before losing control

indicators.note: says the morning piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: a.m. is the morning, the start of the day
fine and OK mean all right

explanation.surface: A sunny morning, before someone lost their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok means behaving wildly and out of control.

clue.text: Split view? Cardi B's predecessor's made up with it!

indicators.note: something made up is invented, its letters put together afresh

parts.note: Cardi B is a rapper; the letter before B is A, giving Cardi A
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gossipy split in a band, with the rapper Cardi B and her forerunner making up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' is the Croatian port, not a breakup, and 'predecessor' moves B back one letter in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic Sea is what you look out on from Split on the Croatian coast.

clue.text: Auden's first away — is at pains to trim the odds

indicators.note: trimming off the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones, taken from away is at pains

explanation.surface: Auden's first poem was absent, and a bookmaker takes pains to shorten the betting odds.
explanation.walkthrough: Count letters through 'away is at pains' and keep the 2nd, 4th, 6th and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden's first name was Wystan, so it is Auden's first.

clue.text: And what have you in your ancient livery?

indicators.note: signals that the list abbreviation goes inside the old word

parts.note: thy is the old form of your
etc. stands for 'and so on', 'and what have you'

explanation.surface: Asking what else hides inside one's old uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'livery' is the adjective meaning irritable (from a bad liver), not a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is an old word for grumpy, peevish, which is what tetchy means.

clue.text: Optimists who, essentially, we will not stop

indicators.note: the two letters will not stay, so they are removed from the combined word

parts.note: per se means in itself, essentially
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hopeful people who believe nothing will halt us.
explanation.walkthrough: W and E, the letters of 'we', are dropped from the ends of WHOPERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopers are people who hope, synonymous with optimists.

clue.text: In work as model or as quizmaster?

definitions.meaning: a model at work is ... for the artist or camera

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is on the job as a model or as a quiz host.
explanation.definitionFit: Posing means holding a position for a portrait, and also putting a question to someone.

clue.text: The day's events I'll announce — from 1100?

parts.note: 1100 in Roman numerals is written with two letters, a thousand and a hundred, and their names spelt as words give the answer

explanation.surface: A host of the day's proceedings, starting at eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '1100' looks like a time on the 24-hour clock; it is the Roman numeral MC.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies introduces each act or item of a programme or event.

clue.text: Deception by bowler? This might result!

definitions.text: Deception by bowler? This might result!

parts.words: Deception by bowler? This might result!
parts.note: read one way it is a conjuring stunt with a bowler hat; read as cricket, a bowler's three wickets with consecutive balls

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler deceives a batsman, and a feat might follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's bowler is the player who delivers the ball; a bowler is also a hard round hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat-trick is three successes in a row, first named for a cricket bowler's three wickets.

clue.text: Old friends think it harms cases

indicators.note: the words around encase, or hold, the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Long-standing friends believe something damages lawsuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Kith, as in 'kith and kin', is an old word for one's friends and acquaintances.

clue.text: Fabian's writing on instruments of the past

indicators.note: in an across clue, writing put on Shaw comes after him

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was a leading member of the socialist Fabian Society
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A Fabian socialist's writings on old musical instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' reads as 'about' but tells you the manuscript follows Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Shawms are medieval and Renaissance double-reed woodwinds, forerunners of the oboe.

clue.text: Feature of initial (and, paradoxically, final) phase

definitions.text: Feature of initial (and, paradoxically, final) phase

indicators.note: something featured in a phrase appears in it, so the answer lies within the two words

explanation.surface: A remark that some characteristic belongs to both the opening and closing stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the opening phase, and paradoxically it lies inside 'final phase'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha, the first Greek letter, stands for the beginning, the initial phase of anything.

clue.text: Failing that's turned around in the days before court game

indicators.note: signals that the turned phrase goes inside the days

parts.note: eves are the evenings or days before events

indicators.note: turning a phrase around reads it backwards

parts.note: 'if not' means failing that

explanation.surface: A fallback plan about to be reversed just before a court date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests law; it is a playing court. Eton fives is played mainly at British public schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton fives is a handball game played in a three-walled court, devised at Eton College.
